newsitem.title: UK: NatWest, SocGen cut British Steel forecasts.
newsitem.headline: NatWest, SocGen cut British Steel forecasts.

text.p: Analysts at SocGen and NatWest Securities confirmed on Thursday that they have joined Merrill Lynch in cutting their profit forecasts for British Steel in the wake of Sterling's strong appreciation against the Deutsche mark.

SocGen analyst Andy Chambers told Reuters he had cut British Steel pretax profit figures for the year to March 1998 to 400 million stg from 700 million. Industry sources also said that NatWest Markets had gone further by also slashing the current year pretax profit forecast to March 1997 to 477 million from 611 million. NatWest has cut the forecast for the following year to 355 million from 449.

This follows Merrill analyst Paul Compton saying earlier that he had more than halved his prediction for the year to March 1998 to 280 million stg from the previous figure of 650 million for pretax profits.
All analysts reported that British Steel would be hit in European export markets which are mark/sterling sensitive.
But as sterling gains ground, its UK market has also become vulnerable through domestic customers buying cheaper mark-denominated imports.
Of British Steel's eight billion stg in sales, 40 percent is exported.
One analyst said he believed the mark would return to around the 2.60 level against stg. It is currently around 2.67 marks.
But so far analysts at UBS, British Steel's brokers, have kept their forecasts unchanged at 750 million stg for the year ending March 1998.
The company itself has not been available to comment on whether sterling gains could indeed slash profits in half.
